newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down on overseas liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down on overseas liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down on Friday due to overseas liquidation ahead of the weekend and trading was dull on bearish market sentiment, brokers said.
The index fell 0.362 points or 0.74 percent to 48.286 percent on volume of 4.4 million shares worth $1.6 million. Of 41 B shares, 34 traded with 21 down, seven flat and six up.
Brokers said the market suffered from overseas selling in selective stocks despite speculative support by some domestic institutions.
"The sluggish market attracted few investors," one broker said.
"The index is approaching the key 48 points support level and it will be tested next week," a second broker said. "If the 48 point is breached, market sentiment will worsen further."
Shanghai Friendship and Overseas Chinese was the worst performer on institutional liquidation, falling $0.018 or 4.52 percent to $0.380 on volume of 36,500 shares.

Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere traded the most on liquidation selling, but one domestic institution supported it in what brokers said appeared to be an effort to help the firm's proposed listing of extra B shares.
It ended unchanged at $0.480 on volume of 515,300 shares.
Shanghai A shares rose on buying of third liners amid good market fundamentals, brokers said.

The A index gained 6.398 points or 0.67 percent to 956.166 points on volume of 1.0 billion shares worth 7.4 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index edged up 1.015 points or 0.04 percent to 2495.814 points.
Chengdu Gongyi Metallurgy was the star on institutional speculative buying, surging 1.91 yuan or 37.37 percent to 7.02 yuan on volume of 28. 5 million shares.
